# `llms.txt` — auto-generated routes

## What it is

`llms.txt` is a curated index of site content targeted at AI agents and LLM crawlers (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, etc.). As of PR shipping `docs/solutions/architecture/llms-txt-automation.md` (2026-05-20) it is **no longer a hand-maintained `public/llms.txt` file** — it is generated by two `force-static` App Router routes that regenerate on every deploy, with no manual maintenance:

- `ethereum.org/llms.txt` → `app/llms.txt/route.ts` — full site index, organized by main-nav top sections.
- `ethereum.org/developers/docs/llms.txt` → `app/developers/docs/llms.txt/route.ts` — developer-docs-only index, organized by the docs sidebar.

The split mirrors `nextjs.org/llms.txt` + `nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt`: the root file points at the docs file rather than inlining 100+ lines of deeply nested developer docs. Shared rendering/frontmatter logic lives in `src/lib/llms-txt/` (`render.ts`, `frontmatter.ts`).

## Why it matters

LLM-powered search tools increasingly fetch `llms.txt` as a discovery root. Keeping it accurate:
- Helps AI agents cite ethereum.org content (improves reach).
- Routes them to the raw markdown, which is lighter and cleaner than the rendered HTML.
- Avoids sending them to 404s when paths change.

## How it updates

**Automatically, on every deploy.** There is no `/update-llms-txt` slash command anymore and no file to hand-edit.

- **Which pages appear** is driven by the **nav files only** (main nav, Footer, developer-docs YAML) — it never walks `public/content/`. So a page appears in `llms.txt` when it is linked from nav, not merely when its markdown exists.
- **Section structure** mirrors the main-nav top sections 1:1 (Learn / Use / Build / Participate / Research) plus Legal & Policies from the Footer's secondary links.

**Implication for changes:** to add/remove a page from `llms.txt`, change what nav links to it — not a static index. If a new top-level page should appear, ensure it's wired into the relevant nav source.

## Gotchas

- **Nav-driven, not content-driven.** A markdown page that exists but isn't linked from nav will not appear. This is intentional.
- **`.md` rewrites still back the linked targets.** Pure App Router routes without a markdown source won't resolve as `.md`; the generator's nav sourcing avoids these by construction, but keep it in mind if you extend the generator.
- **Locale variants are not listed.** Entries point at the default-locale English content only.

## Full design

See `docs/solutions/architecture/llms-txt-automation.md` in the repo for the complete strategy, the nav-sourcing rules, and the `force-static` rationale (same ISR/`public/content`-exclusion trap as the sitemap — see the sitemap section in `SKILL.md`).

## Historical context (for git-blame spelunking)

The pre-automation era hand-maintained `public/llms.txt`; iterative commits `ee5b86e6d5` (initial), `24dee47ff7` (point to `.md`), `a7d57b68f1`, `140fb37a8f`, `a1d43287e6` (path renames). Superseded by the automated routes above.
